items.title: 71231_Sam Wooding Oral History Interview
items.q: Ada Walker was a very clever singer.

ctx.x: But they felt that way. Somebody was singing way down there, 'I Honey love you baby --', it was hoarse and raspy like that, they thought that was good, see?

And so, anyway, Maude DeForrest's partner was Gus Smith -- the guy was successful with moving. And my bunch. Then, we had a couple of comedians on the show, and the rest was -- two dancers. That's about all. But none of them of any consequence. But Gus Smith and Maude deForrest and myself, and Eddie Green, were the biggest people worth mentioning.

items.title: 71231_Sam Wooding Oral History Interview
items.q: George Walker was a dancer, and George's wife was also a dancer and a singer.

ctx.x: Now, well, where I got my inspiration was, when we went to this theater, we saw Williams and Walker. Williams Bert Williams was a great comedian, George Walker was a dancer, and George's wife was also a dancer and a singer.
